svg.aria-label: Layout of an i.MX95 flash.bin with three containers, and where the boot ROM and SPL load each image
svg.title: Inside flash.bin
svg.text: flash.bin · layout from imx-mkimage · not to scale

g.text: image 1: System Manager → M33 TCM · hash
SRK table: up to 4 public keys
each hash ties an image to the signed header
flash.bin is a row of containers. On an SD card it starts at 32 KiB (part 1); offsets here are relative to that start.
The container headers come first, back to back at 1 KiB steps, and the images they describe follow.
The first header, at offset 0, describes one image: the ELE firmware. NXP builds and signs this container, and you
include it unchanged (mx95b0-ahab-container.img for B0 silicon).
The second header, at 0x400, is yours. Its image table lists the OEI, the System Manager and SPL, each with its offset
in flash.bin, size, load address, entry point and hash.
After the image table comes the signature block: a table of up to four public keys (the SRK table), the signature, and
an optional certificate. The signature covers the header, the image table and the key table. The images themselves are
The fuses hold only a hash of the SRK table. Before the ELE trusts any key in a container, it hashes the container's
key table and compares the result with the fuses.
The boot ROM hands the ELE firmware to the ELE. The ELE ROM checks it against NXP's key and starts it; from here on,
the ELE firmware does the checking.
The boot ROM reads the second header and asks the ELE to authenticate it: the key table against the fuse hash, then
Each image then goes to its load address and is checked against its hash. The OEI goes to the M33 TCM and runs first:
it trains the DRAM and returns to the ROM (part 3).
The System Manager goes to the same TCM address and replaces the OEI. SPL goes to OCRAM. The boot ROM's work ends
here: the M33 jumps to the System Manager, which starts the A55 on SPL.
The boot ROM never reads the third container. SPL does: it asks the ELE to authenticate the header, loads TF-A and
U-Boot into the now-trained DRAM, and has each image checked against its hash. SPL only does these checks if U-Boot is
